causal_claim: Transformer architecture made the modern AI agent possible by providing the scalable sequence model that all LLM cores are built on.
definition: A neural network architecture based entirely on self-attention, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions, that became the foundation of modern large language models.
name: Transformer architecture

causal_claim: Self-attention mechanism made the modern AI agent possible by letting its language core relate distant parts of a context in one parallel step, which recurrence could not do at scale.
definition: A mechanism that lets a model weigh the relevance of every token in a sequence against every other token in parallel, replacing sequential recurrence.
name: Self-attention mechanism

causal_claim: Attention mechanism (neural machine translation) made the modern AI agent possible by proving that learned soft alignment over context beats fixed-vector bottlenecks, the direct precursor of transformer self-attention.
definition: Bahdanau-style additive attention, introduced for neural machine translation, which let a decoder focus on relevant source words instead of compressing a sentence into one fixed vector.
name: Attention mechanism (neural machine translation)
source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

causal_claim: Sequence-to-sequence learning made the modern AI agent possible by showing one trainable architecture could convert between arbitrary sequences, the template later generalized into prompt-to-response language modeling.
definition: The encoder-decoder framework that maps an input sequence to an output sequence of different length using recurrent networks, establishing general-purpose sequence transduction.
name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

causal_claim: Long short-term memory (LSTM) made the modern AI agent possible by first making long-sequence learning trainable, the line of work that defined sequence modeling before transformers replaced it.
definition: A recurrent network architecture with gated memory cells that can carry information over long time lags without the gradient vanishing.
name: Long short-term memory (LSTM)

causal_claim: Backpropagation popularized made the modern AI agent possible by giving multi-layer networks a practical training algorithm, without which no LLM core could be fitted to data.
definition: The Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams demonstration that the chain-rule gradient method trains multi-layer networks effectively, turning neural nets into a general learning technology.
name: Backpropagation popularized

causal_claim: Stochastic gradient descent made the modern AI agent possible by making it computationally feasible to optimize billions of parameters on streaming data, the training regime every LLM still uses.
definition: The Robbins-Monro iterative optimization method that updates parameters from noisy single-sample gradient estimates instead of exact batch gradients.
name: Stochastic gradient descent
source_title: A Stochastic Approximation Method (Annals of Mathematical Statistics)

causal_claim: Adam optimizer made the modern AI agent possible by making transformer training stable and nearly tuning-free at scale, a practical precondition for fitting LLM cores.
definition: An adaptive learning-rate optimizer combining momentum and per-parameter scaling that became the default way to train deep networks and transformers.
name: Adam optimizer
source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

causal_claim: Generative pre-training (GPT-1) made the modern AI agent possible by establishing the pretrain-then-adapt recipe that turns raw text into a general-purpose reasoning core.
definition: The demonstration that a transformer language model pre-trained on unlabeled text and then fine-tuned transfers broadly across language tasks.
name: Generative pre-training (GPT-1)
source_title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

causal_claim: BERT masked language modeling made the modern AI agent possible by proving bidirectional pre-trained representations transfer across tasks, the pattern behind the encoders agents use for perception and retrieval.
definition: Bidirectional transformer pre-training by masking and predicting tokens, which set the template for representation-learning encoders used in perception and retrieval.
name: BERT masked language modeling
source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

causal_claim: Scaling laws for neural language models made the modern AI agent possible by telling builders that simply scaling a transformer predictably buys capability, justifying the hundred-million-dollar training runs behind agent cores.
definition: Empirical power laws relating language-model loss predictably to model size, dataset size and compute, which made capability growth plannable.
name: Scaling laws for neural language models
source_title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

causal_claim: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) made the modern AI agent possible by converting a raw text predictor into an instruction-following system a user can actually direct and steer.
definition: Fine-tuning a language model against a reward model learned from human preference comparisons so outputs follow instructions and human intent.
name: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)
source_title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

causal_claim: Instruction tuning made the modern AI agent possible by making the model's interface plain language commands, the control surface every agent loop depends on.
definition: Fine-tuning language models on datasets of instructions paired with desired responses so they generalize to unseen commands phrased in natural language.
name: Instruction tuning
source_title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners (FLAN)

causal_claim: Chain-of-thought prompting made the modern AI agent possible by showing an LLM can externalize step-by-step reasoning in language, the working-memory trick agent loops exploit for planning.
definition: The finding that prompting a large language model to emit intermediate reasoning steps dramatically improves its performance on multi-step problems.
name: Chain-of-thought prompting
source_title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

causal_claim: ReAct (reasoning and acting) made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the canonical reason-act-observe loop structure that defines the modern agent itself.
definition: A prompting paradigm that interleaves verbal reasoning traces with actions and environment observations in one loop.
name: ReAct (reasoning and acting)
source_title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

causal_claim: Toolformer made the modern AI agent possible by showing a language model can learn on its own to invoke calculators, search and other tools, the action channel agents need to affect the world.
definition: A method for language models to teach themselves when and how to call external APIs, inserting tool results into their own text stream.
name: Toolformer
source_title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

causal_claim: Byte-pair encoding tokenization made the modern AI agent possible by giving language models a robust way to convert arbitrary text into tokens, the perception front-end of every LLM core.
definition: Adapting byte-pair encoding as a subword segmentation algorithm so neural models handle open vocabularies with a fixed token set.
name: Byte-pair encoding tokenization
source_title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

causal_claim: Word2vec embeddings made the modern AI agent possible by proving words and concepts can live as vectors a network can compute over, the representational assumption built into every transformer embedding layer.
definition: Efficient methods for learning dense word vectors from raw text in which semantic similarity becomes geometric proximity.
name: Word2vec embeddings
source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

causal_claim: Distributional semantics (Firth's hypothesis) made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the theoretical license to learn meaning from raw text statistics alone, which is exactly what LLM pre-training does.
definition: The principle that a word's meaning is characterized by the company it keeps, i.e. by its distribution across contexts in text.
name: Distributional semantics (Firth's hypothesis)

causal_claim: CLIP vision-language model made the modern AI agent possible by giving agents a perception encoder that speaks the same representational language as their text core.
definition: A model trained contrastively on image-text pairs that aligns visual and linguistic representations in one embedding space, usable zero-shot.
name: CLIP vision-language model
source_title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

causal_claim: Vision Transformer (ViT) made the modern AI agent possible by showing perception can run on the same transformer substrate as language, enabling one architecture to convert between modalities.
definition: Applying the pure transformer architecture to sequences of image patches, unifying vision with the same architecture used for language.
name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
source_title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale

causal_claim: AlexNet made the modern AI agent possible by proving deep networks trained on GPUs decisively beat hand-engineered perception, starting the capability curve agents now ride.
definition: The deep convolutional network trained on GPUs that won ImageNet by a large margin and ignited the deep learning era.
name: AlexNet
source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

causal_claim: ImageNet dataset made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the labeled data and benchmark that made perception trainable and comparable, the data pattern later repeated for language.
definition: A large-scale hand-labeled image database organized by the WordNet hierarchy that gave machine perception a common measurable target.
name: ImageNet dataset
source_title: ImageNet: A Large-Scale Hierarchical Image Database

causal_claim: CUDA made the modern AI agent possible by unlocking the massively parallel hardware without which transformer training at scale is computationally out of reach.
definition: NVIDIA's parallel computing platform that opened GPU hardware to general-purpose computation through a C-like programming model.
name: CUDA

causal_claim: Perceptron made the modern AI agent possible by originating the learnable-neuron paradigm from which every network inside an agent descends.
definition: Rosenblatt's first trainable artificial neural network, a machine that learned classification weights from examples.
name: Perceptron
source_title: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain

causal_claim: Turing's learning machine proposal made the modern AI agent possible by first articulating that intelligence should be trained rather than programmed, the premise the entire agent program inherits.
definition: Turing's proposal in 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' for child machines educated by reward and punishment instead of being fully programmed.
name: Turing's learning machine proposal

causal_claim: Information theory (Shannon) made the modern AI agent possible by founding the quantitative framework of information in which language modeling, cross-entropy loss and token prediction are defined.
definition: Shannon's mathematical theory of communication defining entropy and channel capacity, which made information a measurable quantity.
name: Information theory (Shannon)

causal_claim: Cross-entropy loss made the modern AI agent possible by giving language models their exact training signal: minimize surprise at the next token.
definition: The measure of divergence between a predicted probability distribution and the true one, derived from Shannon entropy and used as the standard training objective for classifiers and language models.
name: Cross-entropy loss

causal_claim: Maximum likelihood estimation made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the estimation principle that next-token training maximizes: the likelihood of real text under the model.
definition: Fisher's principle of choosing the parameters that make the observed data most probable, the statistical foundation of model fitting.
name: Maximum likelihood estimation

causal_claim: Bayesian probability (Bayes' theorem) made the modern AI agent possible by formalizing belief updating from evidence, the inferential stance probabilistic models and agent reasoning approximate.
definition: The rule for updating the probability of a hypothesis as evidence arrives, the formal backbone of reasoning under uncertainty.
name: Bayesian probability (Bayes' theorem)
source_title: An Essay towards solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances

causal_claim: Markov decision process formalism made the modern AI agent possible by defining the mathematical object an acting agent optimizes: a policy over states and actions with cumulative reward.
definition: Bellman's mathematical framework of states, actions, transition probabilities and rewards for sequential decision-making under uncertainty.
name: Markov decision process formalism

causal_claim: Q-learning made the modern AI agent possible by proving an agent can learn what to do purely from reward signals, the learning-from-feedback lineage that RLHF later adapted for language models.
definition: Watkins' model-free reinforcement learning algorithm that learns the value of state-action pairs from experience without a model of the environment.
name: Q-learning
source_title: Learning from Delayed Rewards (thesis, University of Cambridge)

causal_claim: Temporal difference learning made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the bootstrapped value-learning mechanism underlying the reinforcement methods used to align and steer agent behavior.
definition: Sutton's method of learning predictions by bootstrapping from later predictions, the core update rule of modern reinforcement learning.
name: Temporal difference learning
source_title: Learning to Predict by the Methods of Temporal Differences

causal_claim: Monte Carlo tree search made the modern AI agent possible by demonstrating that learned models plus lookahead search produce superhuman sequential decisions, the planning pattern agent architectures imitate.
definition: A search algorithm that builds a decision tree guided by random simulation outcomes, famously powering AlphaGo's move selection.
name: Monte Carlo tree search

causal_claim: Statistical learning theory (VC dimension) made the modern AI agent possible by first making 'learning from finite data' a rigorous science, the intellectual frame in which training a model to generalize is understood.
definition: Vapnik and Chervonenkis's theory bounding generalization error by a capacity measure of a hypothesis class, founding the mathematics of learning from data.
name: Statistical learning theory (VC dimension)

causal_claim: Universal approximation theorem made the modern AI agent possible by guaranteeing that neural networks are expressive enough in principle to represent the mappings agents need, justifying the bet on scale.
definition: Cybenko's proof that a feedforward network with a single hidden layer can approximate any continuous function on a compact set.
name: Universal approximation theorem
source_title: Approximation by superpositions of a sigmoidal function

causal_claim: Stored-program architecture made the modern AI agent possible by creating the general-purpose computer on which every model, tool and agent loop physically runs.
definition: The von Neumann design in which instructions and data share one memory, making the computer a universal, reprogrammable machine.
name: Stored-program architecture
source_title: First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC

causal_claim: ImageNet made the modern AI agent possible by proving large labeled datasets plus benchmarks could train and measure perception systems at scale, the pattern later reused for language model evaluation.
definition: A large-scale image database of over 14 million hand-annotated images organized by the WordNet hierarchy, built to benchmark visual recognition.
name: ImageNet

causal_claim: The ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge made the modern AI agent possible by creating the annual benchmark competition whose 2012 result demonstrated deep learning's superiority and redirected the field.
definition: An annual computer vision competition (2010-2017) evaluating algorithms on ImageNet object detection and classification tasks.
name: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC)

causal_claim: GLUE benchmark made the modern AI agent possible by giving language models a shared measurable target for general understanding, driving the encoder era whose models agents now build on.
definition: The General Language Understanding Evaluation benchmark, a collection of nine sentence- and sentence-pair understanding tasks for training and evaluating NLP models.
name: GLUE benchmark

causal_claim: CUDA made the modern AI agent possible by turning GPUs into general-purpose parallel computers programmable in C, the platform on which essentially all large model training runs.
definition: NVIDIA's parallel computing platform and programming model that lets developers use GPUs for general-purpose computation.
name: CUDA

causal_claim: The tensor processing unit made the modern AI agent possible by showing custom silicon for tensor algebra could cut the cost of training and serving large neural networks by an order of magnitude.
definition: Google's custom ASIC designed to accelerate machine learning workloads, first used internally in 2015 and announced in 2016.
name: Tensor processing unit (TPU)

causal_claim: Amazon Web Services made the modern AI agent possible by making elastic compute rentable by the hour, so training runs and agent hosting no longer required owning a data center.
definition: Amazon's cloud computing platform, launched in 2006 with S3 and EC2, offering on-demand compute and storage over the internet.
name: Amazon Web Services

causal_claim: Git made the modern AI agent possible by becoming the version control substrate of the open-source ecosystem whose code and collaboration produced the frameworks agents are built with.
definition: Linus Torvalds' distributed version control system, created in 2005 for Linux kernel development.
name: Git

causal_claim: GitHub made the modern AI agent possible by centralizing open-source collaboration, hosting the code, issues, and training corpora that the agent ecosystem is built from.
definition: A web-based platform for version control and collaborative software development built on Git, launched in 2008.
name: GitHub

causal_claim: The point-contact transistor made the modern AI agent possible by replacing vacuum tubes with a solid-state switch, the device from which all digital computing hardware descends.
definition: The first working transistor, demonstrated by Bardeen and Brattain at Bell Labs in December 1947 using a germanium point-contact design.
name: Point-contact transistor

causal_claim: The silicon transistor made the modern AI agent possible by making transistors cheap, rugged, and manufacturable, turning computing hardware into a mass-produced commodity.
definition: The first silicon transistor, produced by Gordon Teal at Texas Instruments in 1954, replacing fragile germanium devices.
name: Silicon transistor

causal_claim: The planar process made the modern AI agent possible by making transistors printable in batches on a flat wafer, the manufacturing step that let chips scale.
definition: Jean Hoerni's 1957-1959 process of building transistors under a protective silicon oxide layer on a flat wafer surface.
name: Planar process

causal_claim: The integrated circuit made the modern AI agent possible by putting whole circuits on one chip, collapsing cost and size so computing could scale for decades.
definition: A set of electronic circuits on one small flat piece of semiconductor material, independently demonstrated by Kilby (1958) and Noyce (1959).
name: Integrated circuit

causal_claim: The Czochralski process made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the large, near-perfect silicon single crystals from which virtually all semiconductor wafers are cut.
definition: A method of crystal growth, adapted to silicon in the 1950s, that pulls a large single crystal from molten material using a seed crystal.
name: Czochralski process

causal_claim: Zone refining made the modern AI agent possible by achieving the ultra-pure semiconductor material without which reliable transistors cannot be made.
definition: William Pfann's technique of passing molten zones along a rod to sweep impurities to one end, purifying semiconductor material.
name: Zone refining

causal_claim: The MOSFET made the modern AI agent possible by becoming the scalable, low-power switch of which modern processors and AI accelerators contain tens of billions.
definition: The metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor, demonstrated by Kahng and Atalla at Bell Labs in 1959 and now the most manufactured device in history.
name: MOSFET

causal_claim: Photolithography made the modern AI agent possible by providing the printing technique that shrinks transistor features generation after generation.
definition: A process using light to transfer a geometric pattern from a photomask to a light-sensitive chemical photoresist on a substrate.
name: Photolithography

causal_claim: Probability axioms (Kolmogorov) made the modern AI agent possible by giving uncertainty a rigorous calculus on which statistical learning and probabilistic model outputs rest.
definition: Andrey Kolmogorov's 1933 axiomatization of probability theory on measure-theoretic foundations in 'Foundations of the Theory of Probability'.
name: Probability axioms (Kolmogorov)
source_title: Foundations of the Theory of Probability - Wikipedia

causal_claim: Matrix calculus and linear algebra made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the mathematical language in which neural network computation is expressed as tensor operations.
definition: The body of linear algebra (vectors, matrices, transformations) formalized in the 19th-20th centuries and used to express computation in modern computing.
name: Linear algebra (matrix calculus)

causal_claim: The gradient descent algorithm made the modern AI agent possible by giving an iterative rule for minimizing a loss function, the engine of all neural network training.
definition: A first-order iterative optimization algorithm for finding a local minimum of a differentiable function, rooted in Cauchy's 1847 method.
name: Gradient descent

causal_claim: Stochastic gradient descent made the modern AI agent possible by making optimization over massive datasets tractable through noisy minibatch updates instead of full-batch gradients.
definition: An iterative method for optimizing an objective function using gradient estimates from random subsets of data, from Robbins and Monro's 1951 stochastic approximation.
name: Stochastic gradient descent

causal_claim: A Mathematical Theory of Communication made the modern AI agent possible by defining information, entropy, and cross-entropy, the quantities that language model training literally optimizes.
definition: Claude Shannon's 1948 paper founding information theory, introducing entropy and the noisy channel model.
name: Information theory (Shannon)
source_title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication - Wikipedia

causal_claim: Bayes' theorem made the modern AI agent possible by formalizing how beliefs update with evidence, the inferential stance behind probabilistic models and agent reasoning under uncertainty.
definition: The rule describing the probability of an event based on prior knowledge of conditions related to it, published posthumously in 1763 from Bayes' essay.
name: Bayes' theorem

causal_claim: Monte Carlo method made the modern AI agent possible by showing intractable integrals and expectations could be estimated by random sampling, a technique used throughout training and evaluation.
definition: A class of computational algorithms relying on repeated random sampling, developed by Ulam, von Neumann, and Metropolis in the 1940s.
name: Monte Carlo method

causal_claim: Boolean algebra made the modern AI agent possible by reducing logic to algebra, the formal basis on which digital circuits and computation are built.
definition: George Boole's 1854 'An Investigation of the Laws of Thought', introducing an algebraic system of logic with true/false values.
name: Boolean algebra

causal_claim: ARPANET made the modern AI agent possible by proving packet-switched networking worked, creating the network lineage that became the internet agents operate over.
definition: The first wide-area packet-switched network with distributed control, first deployed in 1969, and a direct predecessor of the internet.
name: ARPANET

causal_claim: TCP/IP made the modern AI agent possible by standardizing how networks interoperate, creating the single global network through which agents perceive and act.
definition: The Internet protocol suite, designed by Cerf and Kahn in 1974 and adopted as the ARPANET standard on January 1, 1983.
name: TCP/IP

causal_claim: World Wide Web made the modern AI agent possible by creating the hyperlinked document space that became both the largest text corpus for training and the environment agents browse and act in.
definition: Tim Berners-Lee's 1989-1991 system of interlinked hypertext documents accessed via the internet, built at CERN.
name: World Wide Web

causal_claim: Common Crawl made the modern AI agent possible by giving any lab a free, web-scale text corpus, the raw material from which GPT-class models are trained.
definition: A nonprofit that crawls the web and freely provides petabytes of web page data, founded in 2007 and widely used to train language models.
name: Common Crawl

causal_claim: The Linux operating system made the modern AI agent possible by becoming the free operating system running essentially all training clusters, servers, and data centers.
definition: Linus Torvalds' free Unix-like operating system kernel, first released in 1991, now dominant in servers and supercomputing.
name: Linux operating system

causal_claim: Python made the modern AI agent possible by becoming the lingua franca in which the frameworks, experiments, and agent scaffolding are written.
definition: Guido van Rossum's high-level programming language, first released in 1991, now the dominant language of machine learning research.
name: Python (programming language)

causal_claim: arXiv made the modern AI agent possible by collapsing the delay between discovery and global scrutiny to days, letting agent techniques spread and compound at preprint speed.
definition: An open-access archive of electronic preprints founded by Paul Ginsparg in 1991, the primary rapid-dissemination channel for ML research.
name: arXiv

causal_claim: Wikipedia made the modern AI agent possible by creating a vast, structured, freely licensed text corpus that anchors language model knowledge and evaluation.
definition: The free online encyclopedia launched in 2001, written collaboratively by volunteers and used as a core training corpus for language models.
name: Wikipedia

causal_claim: Perceptron made the modern AI agent possible by establishing the learnable weighted-neuron unit that all deep networks, and therefore every LLM behind an agent, are built from.
definition: Rosenblatt's perceptron was the first trainable artificial neural network, learning classification weights from examples on the Mark I Perceptron machine.
name: Perceptron

causal_claim: Backpropagation made the modern AI agent possible by giving multi-layer networks an efficient training algorithm, without which transformer-scale models could not be fitted to data.
definition: The Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams paper popularized training multi-layer neural networks by propagating error gradients backwards through the network.
name: Backpropagation
source_title: Learning representations by back-propagating errors - Nature

causal_claim: Linnainmaa's automatic differentiation made the modern AI agent possible by originating reverse-mode differentiation, the exact gradient computation that backpropagation and all modern deep learning frameworks perform.
definition: Seppo Linnainmaa's 1970 master's thesis gave the first efficient representation of the derivative of a nested function, the reverse mode of automatic differentiation.
name: Linnainmaa's automatic differentiation
source_title: The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors

causal_claim: Distributional hypothesis made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the linguistic principle that meaning can be learned from context statistics, the foundation of word embeddings and LLM training.
definition: Zellig Harris's distributional hypothesis holds that words occurring in similar contexts have similar meanings, grounding semantics in co-occurrence statistics.
name: Distributional hypothesis

causal_claim: Word2vec made the modern AI agent possible by proving words could be embedded as dense vectors learned from raw text at scale, the representation scheme transformers inherit and generalize.
definition: Mikolov and colleagues' word2vec learns dense vector embeddings of words from large corpora so that semantic relations become vector arithmetic.
name: Word2vec
source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space - arXiv

causal_claim: Energy-based model (Hopfield network / Boltzmann machine) made the modern AI agent possible by importing physics energy-minimization into learning, a lineage that leads to modern probabilistic and attention-like associative memory models.
definition: Hopfield networks and Boltzmann machines imported statistical-physics energy functions into neural computation, treating network states as energy minima.
name: Energy-based model (Hopfield network / Boltzmann machine)

causal_claim: Simulated annealing made the modern AI agent possible by showing physical processes could be turned into optimization algorithms, part of the physics-to-learning transfer that shaped stochastic training methods.
definition: Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi adapted the metallurgical annealing process, via the Metropolis algorithm, into a general method for combinatorial optimization.
name: Simulated annealing

causal_claim: Bayesian network made the modern AI agent possible by formalizing probabilistic reasoning over structured variables, the statistics-derived framework for decision-making under uncertainty that agent planning builds on.
definition: Judea Pearl's Bayesian networks represent probabilistic dependencies as directed graphs, enabling principled reasoning under uncertainty.
name: Bayesian network
source_title: Fusion, propagation, and structuring in belief networks - ACM Digital Library

causal_claim: Markov decision process made the modern AI agent possible by giving the mathematical definition of an agent acting over time, the object every reinforcement-learning-trained agent policy optimizes.
definition: Bellman's Markov decision process formalizes sequential decision-making as states, actions, transition probabilities and rewards.
name: Markov decision process

causal_claim: Optimal control theory (dynamic programming) made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the value-function and Bellman-equation machinery that reinforcement learning, and hence RLHF-tuned agents, directly inherit.
definition: Richard Bellman's dynamic programming decomposes sequential decisions into nested subproblems, founding optimal control and value-function methods.
name: Optimal control theory (dynamic programming)

causal_claim: AlphaGo made the modern AI agent possible by demonstrating that learned models plus search could plan and act superhumanly in a complex environment, the template for agentic reasoning-and-acting systems.
definition: DeepMind's AlphaGo combined deep policy and value networks with Monte Carlo tree search to defeat a top human Go professional.
name: AlphaGo
source_title: Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search - Nature

causal_claim: Dropout made the modern AI agent possible by making very large networks trainable without catastrophic overfitting, a precondition for scaling to LLM size.
definition: Dropout randomly disables units during training, preventing co-adaptation and dramatically improving generalization of large neural networks.
name: Dropout
source_title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting - JMLR

causal_claim: Adam optimizer made the modern AI agent possible by making stochastic gradient training of huge networks stable and practical, the optimizer used to train nearly every production LLM.
definition: Adam is an adaptive stochastic optimization algorithm combining momentum and per-parameter learning rates, published by Kingma and Ba.
name: Adam optimizer
source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization - arXiv

causal_claim: Byte-pair encoding tokenization made the modern AI agent possible by giving LLMs a robust way to convert arbitrary text into model tokens, the input layer every agent's reasoning depends on.
definition: Sennrich, Haddow and Birch adapted byte-pair encoding to subword segmentation so neural models can handle open vocabularies with a fixed token set.
name: Byte-pair encoding tokenization
source_title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units - arXiv

causal_claim: Attention mechanism (Bahdanau) made the modern AI agent possible by introducing learned soft alignment over context, the mechanism transformers later generalized into self-attention.
definition: Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio introduced additive attention, letting a decoder dynamically focus on relevant source words during translation.
name: Attention mechanism (Bahdanau)
source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate - arXiv

causal_claim: Sequence-to-sequence learning made the modern AI agent possible by establishing the encoder-decoder paradigm of mapping arbitrary text in to arbitrary text out, the shape of every LLM interaction.
definition: Sutskever, Vinyals and Le showed an LSTM encoder-decoder could map input sequences to output sequences end-to-end for machine translation.
name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks - arXiv

causal_claim: Transformer architecture made the modern AI agent possible by providing the scalable, parallelizable architecture on which every frontier LLM, and thus every LLM agent, is built.
definition: The Transformer dispenses with recurrence entirely, building sequence models from self-attention, and became the architecture of all modern LLMs.
name: Transformer architecture
source_title: Attention Is All You Need - arXiv

causal_claim: Generative pre-training (GPT-1) made the modern AI agent possible by establishing the pretrain-then-adapt recipe that produces general-purpose language models from raw text.
definition: OpenAI's GPT-1 showed unsupervised generative pre-training of a transformer followed by fine-tuning transfers across language tasks.
name: Generative pre-training (GPT-1)
source_title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training - OpenAI

causal_claim: BERT made the modern AI agent possible by demonstrating that self-supervised pretraining yields transferable language understanding, validating the foundation-model approach agents rely on.
definition: BERT pretrains deep bidirectional transformer representations with masked language modeling and next-sentence prediction.
name: BERT
source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding - arXiv

causal_claim: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) made the modern AI agent possible by converting raw text predictors into instruction-following systems that can be directed, corrected and safely looped by a user.
definition: InstructGPT applied RLHF, training a reward model from human comparisons and optimizing the language model against it with PPO, to make GPT-3 follow instructions.
name: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)
source_title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback - arXiv

causal_claim: Instruction tuning (FLAN) made the modern AI agent possible by teaching models to treat natural-language instructions as their control interface, the channel through which users and agent scaffolds direct them.
definition: FLAN showed that fine-tuning a language model on a mixture of tasks phrased as natural-language instructions yields strong zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks.
name: Instruction tuning (FLAN)
source_title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners - arXiv

causal_claim: Chain-of-thought prompting made the modern AI agent possible by revealing that LLMs can externalize step-by-step reasoning in text, the working-memory mechanism agent loops exploit for planning.
definition: Wei and colleagues showed that prompting large language models to emit intermediate reasoning steps greatly improves multi-step problem solving.
name: Chain-of-thought prompting
source_title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models - arXiv

causal_claim: ReAct agent pattern made the modern AI agent possible by defining the reason-act-observe loop that is the literal architecture of today's LLM agents.
definition: ReAct interleaves language-model reasoning traces with actions and observations, so the model can plan, call tools, and revise based on feedback.
name: ReAct agent pattern
source_title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models - arXiv

causal_claim: ELIZA made the modern AI agent possible by demonstrating that humans will interact with machines conversationally through natural language, the interaction premise of every chat-based agent.
definition: Joseph Weizenbaum's ELIZA simulated a psychotherapist with pattern-matching rules, the first widely known conversational program.
name: ELIZA

causal_claim: Shakey the Robot made the modern AI agent possible by first closing the perceive-plan-act loop in one system, the functional architecture modern agents reimplement in software.
definition: SRI's Shakey was the first mobile robot to perceive its environment, build a model of it, plan, and execute actions to achieve goals.
name: Shakey the Robot
source_title: Shakey the Robot - CHM Revolution Exhibit

causal_claim: Lisp programming language made the modern AI agent possible by creating the symbolic-programming substrate in which the first agent-like reasoning systems were built and prototyped.
definition: John McCarthy's Lisp introduced symbolic list processing, recursion and garbage collection as the native medium of early AI research.
name: Lisp programming language
source_title: Recursive Functions of Symbolic Expressions and Their Computation by Machine, Part I - ACM

causal_claim: Logic Theorist made the modern AI agent possible by demonstrating that a machine could carry out heuristic search over symbolic goals, the first concrete instance of automated reasoning.
definition: Newell, Shaw and Simon's Logic Theorist was the first program designed to mimic human problem-solving, proving theorems from Principia Mathematica.
name: Logic Theorist
source_title: The Logic Theory Machine - Newell & Simon (1956)

causal_claim: Dartmouth Workshop made the modern AI agent possible by founding artificial intelligence as an organized research field whose research programs produced every later agent technology.
definition: The 1956 Dartmouth summer workshop coined 'artificial intelligence' and convened the field's founders around the conjecture that intelligence can be simulated by machines.
name: Dartmouth Workshop
source_title: A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence

causal_claim: Expert systems (DENDRAL/MYCIN) made the modern AI agent possible by proving machines could be deployed as task-performing knowledge agents, the commercial ancestor of today's task agents.
definition: DENDRAL and later MYCIN encoded expert knowledge as rule bases that could reason about chemistry and medical diagnosis at expert level in narrow domains.
name: Expert systems (DENDRAL/MYCIN)

causal_claim: Prolog made the modern AI agent possible by showing declarative goal-directed inference could be mechanized, a direct ancestor of the goal-and-plan machinery in agent architectures.
definition: Prolog is a logic programming language built on Horn clauses, where programs state facts and rules and the interpreter performs automated inference.
name: Prolog
source_title: The Birth of Prolog - Colmerauer & Roussel

causal_claim: Turing Test proposal made the modern AI agent possible by framing machine intelligence as conversational behavior, the criterion chat-based agents are still implicitly judged against.
definition: Alan Turing's 1950 paper proposed the imitation game as an operational test of machine intelligence and anticipated learning machines.
name: Turing Test proposal

causal_claim: McCulloch-Pitts neuron made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the first formal unit of neural computation from which all network models of learning descend.
definition: McCulloch and Pitts modeled neurons as threshold logic units, the first mathematical model of an artificial neural network.
name: McCulloch-Pitts neuron
source_title: A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity - Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics

causal_claim: General Problem Solver made the modern AI agent possible by introducing means-ends analysis, the goal-directed planning schema that agent architectures still instantiate.
definition: Newell, Shaw and Simon's General Problem Solver attacked problems by means-ends analysis, reducing differences between current and goal states.
name: General Problem Solver
source_title: Report on a general problem-solving program - ACM Digital Library

causal_claim: Deep Blue made the modern AI agent possible by proving a machine could out-perform the best human at a flagship intellectual task through search, legitimizing machine agency in adversarial domains.
definition: IBM's Deep Blue defeated world champion Garry Kasparov using massively parallel alpha-beta search and hand-tuned evaluation.
name: Deep Blue

causal_claim: TD-Gammon made the modern AI agent possible by first proving an agent can reach expert performance by learning from its own experience, the self-improvement loop at the heart of RL-trained agents.
definition: Tesauro's TD-Gammon learned world-class backgammon play purely by self-play temporal-difference reinforcement learning.
name: TD-Gammon
source_title: Practical Issues in Temporal Difference Learning - Springer

causal_claim: Speech recognition (Dragon NaturallySpeaking) made the modern AI agent possible by opening the voice channel through which users now direct agents hands-free.
definition: Dragon NaturallySpeaking was the first general-purpose continuous speech recognition product for dictation on personal computers.
name: Speech recognition (Dragon NaturallySpeaking)

causal_claim: Siri made the modern AI agent possible by normalizing the consumer expectation of a conversational assistant that takes actions on your behalf, the market category LLM agents now fulfill.
definition: Apple's Siri brought a voice-controlled personal assistant that interprets natural language and delegates to services to a mass consumer device.
name: Siri

causal_claim: Watson (Jeopardy!) made the modern AI agent possible by demonstrating machine question-answering over open-domain natural language at champion level, a direct functional precursor of knowledge agents.
definition: IBM Watson defeated Jeopardy! champions by combining massive evidence retrieval with probabilistic answer scoring over unstructured text.
name: Watson (Jeopardy!)
source_title: This is Watson - IBM Journal of Research and Development
